title: Local SEO for Home Improvement: 7 Steps to Win the Map Pack
html:
Local SEO for home improvement comes down to 7 steps: complete your Google Business Profile, post project photos weekly, earn reviews every week, build a page for each service and city, keep your business details identical everywhere, earn local links, and track the calls your profile brings in.

Homeowners pick remodelers, roofers, and painters from the top 3 map results more than anywhere else on Google. Each step below moves you closer to that spot. Check your profile chat setup now that Maps shows a Message button next to Call.

1. Complete Your Google Business Profile

Your Google Business Profile (GBP) decides whether you show up in the map pack. An incomplete profile loses to one that answers every question.

- Pick the most specific primary category, like "Bathroom remodeler" or "Kitchen remodeler," not just "Remodeler."
- Add every service you offer, each with a short description.
- Set your service area to the cities you actually drive to.
- Keep regular and holiday hours current.
- Write a description that names your main services and your home city in plain language.

2. Post New Project Photos Every Week

New photos show Google your business is active, and they show homeowners real work instead of stock images.

Upload 3 to 5 photos a week: before-and-after shots, your crew on site, and your branded trucks. Name each file for what it shows, like "kitchen-remodel-naperville.jpg," before you upload it.

Pair the photos with a weekly GBP post about a finished job. One sentence on the project and the city is enough.

5. Keep Your Business Details Identical Everywhere

Google checks your name, address, and phone number (NAP) across the web. If one directory lists an old address, it weakens trust in your profile.

List your business on Angi, Houzz, Yelp, Nextdoor, the BBB, Bing Places, and Apple Business Connect. Use the exact same name, address, and phone format on each one.

Check your listings twice a year, and after any move or phone change.

6. Earn Links From Local Sites

Links from local sites tell Google you're part of the community. They also send real referral traffic.

Ask your suppliers to list you on their "find an installer" or dealer pages. Join your chamber of commerce. Sponsor a youth team or a home show. Each one usually comes with a link back to your site.

7. Track Calls, Not Just Rankings

Rankings mean nothing if the phone doesn't ring. Check your GBP Performance report each month for calls, website clicks, and direction requests.

Add a tracking tag to the website link on your profile, like ?utm_source=GBP, so you can see those visits in Google Analytics. Then compare months, not days, since map rankings move slowly.

How long does local SEO take for a home improvement business?

 Most home improvement businesses see map ranking gains in 1 to 3 months after completing their Google Business Profile and fixing their citations. City pages and local links take longer, usually 3 to 6 months. Competitive services like kitchen remodeling in big metros take the longest.

What's the difference between local SEO and regular SEO?

 Local SEO gets you into the map pack and "near me" results in your service area. It relies on your Google Business Profile, reviews, and citations. Regular SEO ranks your website pages in the standard results, based on content, site speed, and links. Home improvement businesses need both.

How much does local SEO cost for a home improvement business?

Local SEO on its own usually runs $500 to $1,500 a month. That covers Google Business Profile management, review requests, citation cleanup, and a few city pages. Full SEO with content and link building costs more. A single-location business can start at the low end and scale up.
